summary: Defines the describes link relation type, which lets a resource representation indicate that it describes another resource. It is the opposite direction of the describedby relation. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A web page can say I am the description of that other thing. It is the opposite of a thing saying here is my description.

questions: what is the describes link relation
how to use describes link relation
subtitle: The 'describes' link relation type for web resources.

tldr.problem: Web resources need a way to establish associations with their descriptions, but the existing 'describedby' relation only works in one direction: from the described resource to the description.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6892 registers the 'describes' link relation type, which is the inverse of 'describedby': a description resource can link to the resource it describes.
tldr.outcome: Web services can now represent description relationships from both directions, making it easier for applications to discover and associate described resources and their descriptions.

today: RFC 6892 is an Informational RFC and has not been obsoleted. The 'describes' link relation type is registered with IANA and used in web applications to associate description resources with the resources they describe.

sections.title: Link Relations on the Web
sections.content:
Web resources—pages, files, data—can be linked to other resources to represent relationships between them. A link relation type describes what that relationship means. For example, the 'author' relation says one resource is the author of another. The 'describedby' relation, already registered in the IANA registry, means a resource points to something that describes it.

RFC 6892 registers a new link relation type: 'describes'. This is the inverse of 'describedby': instead of the described resource pointing to its description, the description points to what it describes. This gives applications the freedom to represent the relationship from either direction.
sections.eli5: Web pages use special links to say what they are related to. This adds a new kind of link that says I am a description of something else.

sections.title: Describing Resources
sections.content:
In many web applications, one resource describes another. For instance, a document might have metadata about it written in Resource Description Framework (RDF), or a service might provide JSON or XML descriptions of its resources. The 'describes' link relation lets description resources explicitly associate themselves with the resources they describe.

The 'describes' relation has no constraints on format or representation—the described resource and description resource can use any media type. A description resource can even describe multiple resources, or point to another resource that in turn describes something else, creating chains of descriptions.

Together, 'describes' and 'describedby' provide a complete framework: a described resource can point to its description with 'describedby', and a description resource can point back to what it describes with 'describes'.
sections.eli5: One web thing can point to another thing and say I explain that. No matter what format or type of thing, the link means the same thing.

sections.title: Trust and Authority
sections.content:
A 'describes' link does not guarantee the description is authoritative, accurate, or trustworthy. Anyone can create a link saying they describe a resource, but that does not make it true. Resources can have multiple—even conflicting—descriptions.

Applications must not treat description resources as authoritative without additional context. Before trusting a description, a client needs to know who provided both the description resource and the link itself, and must evaluate their authority. Security and trust frameworks are needed to distinguish trusted descriptions from misleading or unauthorized ones.
sections.eli5: Just because a link says something describes something does not mean it is telling the truth. You have to check who is saying it and whether you trust them.
